prompt: Write 5 short claim log entries by an auto insurance adjuster for a low-speed head-on collision claim. Injury: wrist fracture. The claimant is not represented by a lawyer. Start each entry on a new line with 'Entry 1:', 'Entry 2:' and so on. No names, dates or amounts. (Internal reference C-1265; do not mention it.)
text:
Entry 1: Claim received by phone from the insured driver reporting a low-speed head-on collision at an intersection. Driver states the other vehicle crossed the center line while turning. Both vehicles drivable from scene. Police report requested and file opened.

Entry 2: Recorded statement taken from the claimant. Claimant reports a wrist fracture from bracing against the steering wheel and is currently seeking medical treatment. Claimant confirmed no attorney is representing them at this time. Explained the claims process and provided contact information for follow-up questions.

Entry 3: Reviewed photos submitted by both drivers. Minor front bumper damage on the insured vehicle and moderate front-end damage on the claimant vehicle. Airbag deployment noted on the claimant vehicle. Repair estimate requested from the preferred shop network.

Entry 4: Spoke with the claimant's treating provider's office to request medical records related to the wrist fracture. Authorization form sent to the claimant for signature. Bodily injury claim noted as pending medical documentation. Claimant advised that a case reserve will be set once records are received.

Entry 5: Follow-up call with the claimant. Claimant reports cast in place and limited grip strength, with ongoing physical therapy scheduled. Reminded claimant that medical bills and wage loss documentation are needed to evaluate the injury claim. Liability review remains open pending the police report and the other driver's statement.
